issue.title: BUG: HDFStore.select with where, start/stop and chunksize returns wrong rows
issue.body:
### Pandas version checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/whatsnew/index.html) of pandas.

- [ ] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [main branch](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/dev/getting_started/install.html#installing-the-development-version-of-pandas) of pandas.

### Reproducible Example

```python
import os
import tempfile

import pandas as pd

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    path = os.path.join(tmp, "store.h5")
    with pd.HDFStore(path, mode="w") as store:
        store.append("x", pd.DataFrame({"a": range(20)}), format="table", data_columns=True)
        kw = {"where": "a > 3", "start": 10, "stop": 15}
        plain = store.select("x", **kw)["a"].tolist()
        chunked = pd.concat(store.select("x", chunksize=2, **kw))["a"].tolist()
        iterated = pd.concat(store.select("x", iterator=True, **kw))["a"].tolist()

print("select(where='a > 3', start=10, stop=15):", plain)
print("same with chunksize=2:                   ", chunked)
print("same with iterator=True:                 ", iterated)
print("expected for all three:                  ", [10, 11, 12, 13, 14])
```

### Issue Description

`store.select(key, where=..., start=10, stop=15)` returns rows 10 to 14, but the same call with `chunksize=2` or `iterator=True` returns rows 14 to 18, which lie outside the requested window.

Output on 3.0.6 (tables 3.11.1):

```
select(where='a > 3', start=10, stop=15): [10, 11, 12, 13, 14]
same with chunksize=2:                    [14, 15, 16, 17, 18]
same with iterator=True:                  [14, 15, 16, 17, 18]
expected for all three:                   [10, 11, 12, 13, 14]
```

In `TableIterator` (`pandas/io/pytables.py` at 03e5d938ad), `get_result` reads the matching coordinates over the whole table with `read_coordinates(where=self.where)` and no start or stop (2600), and `__iter__` then slices that result with `self.coordinates[current:stop]` where `current` starts at `self.start` (2567, 2576). So the start/stop window is applied to the list of matching rows rather than to the table. The non-chunked path passes `start` and `stop` to `read_coordinates`, which matches the `select_as_coordinates` docstring. #65598 last touched this code but the behaviour is the same in 3.0.6. No test combines `chunksize` or `iterator` with both `where` and `start`/`stop`.

Passing `start=self.start, stop=self.stop` to `read_coordinates` and iterating the returned coordinates from position 0 would make the chunked path match the non-chunked one.

I ran this on pandas 3.0.6. I have not run it on a main build, but the code cited above is unchanged on main at 03e5d938ad.

### Expected Behavior

All three calls return `[10, 11, 12, 13, 14]`.
